column1: # Pin changelog for the Kalamari curation-triage tool -- the record behind point 4
# of the update gate (bin/curation-triage/update_gate.py).
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# A Tier-2 verdict is only worth reading if a reader can tell why it says what it
# says.  Four kinds of thing move a call: the software, the database it reads, a
# threshold, and our own reading rule.  This file records every identity each of
# those has ever had, so a changed call can always be attributed to something.  A
# call that changes while nothing here moved is `unattributable`, and that is a
# FAILURE, not a fifth category: it means the same pins produced two different
# answers.  `unattributable` is therefore rejected as a value of the class column.
# HOW IT IS CHECKED
# `python3 bin/curation-triage/update_gate.py --check` (what CI runs, fully offline)
# compares every component's current identity with the LAST `to` recorded here.  A
# pin that moved without a new row fails the gate, and the failure names the row to
# add.  Each component's rows also have to form an unbroken chain: the first row
# starts from `-`, and every later row starts where the previous one ended.
# COLUMNS
#   date                 YYYY-MM-DD, append-ordered (rows never go backwards in time)
#   component            what moved: tool:<env> | db:<env> | threshold:<x> | rule:<x>
#                        | panel:scope (which units the validation panel replays)
#   class                software | database | threshold | rule | panel
#                        (never unattributable)
#   from                 the identity before this row; `-` means there was no pin
#   to                   the identity after this row; `-` means the pin was removed
#   panel_calls_total    calls in the validation panel when this row was accepted
#   panel_calls_changed  how many of them this change moved
#   validation           panel-replay:<12 hex>, the digest of the accepted call table
#   reviewer             who signed for it
#   note                 why, in a sentence a reader who was not there can use
# A software identity is `<conda build>+lock:<first 12 hex of the lockfile sha256>`.
# Both halves are needed: the build alone misses a dependency bump that reinstalls
# half the prefix, and the digest alone is unreadable here.  The full 64-hex digest
# lives in tool_pins.tsv, which point 1 of the gate checks against the file on disk.
# A DATABASE IDENTITY IS WHAT THE DATABASE CALLS ITSELF -- AND FOR THE ONE DATABASE
# THAT LIVES OUTSIDE ITS PACKAGE, A NAME IS NOT EVIDENCE
# db:amrfinderplus is recorded as `2026-05-15.1`, the string
# `amrfinder --database_version` prints.  That is a LABEL: any directory can be given
# that name, `amrfinder -u` only ever fetches the LATEST database, and no command
# anywhere asks NCBI for a dated one.  So on 2026-08-04 that database was FROZEN --
# all 162 of its files (239.4 MB) digested one per line into
# src/curation-triage/amrfinderplus_db_manifest.tsv, with a single roll-up sha256
# 2fb16b7f3c57... over the sorted (name, hash) pairs.  The roll-up is recorded as
# database_digest in tool_pins.tsv, and setup_envs.sh now compares the installed
# database against that manifest file by file instead of trusting the version string.
# The digest is PART OF the db:amrfinderplus identity, so the gate itself catches a
# database swapped underneath an unchanged version string -- not only setup_envs.sh.
# `update_gate.database_identity` builds db:<env> as
# `<database_version>+db:<first 12 hex of database_digest>`, which is why the row below
# reads `2026-05-15.1+db:2fb16b7f3c57` while `amrfinder --database_version` still prints
# the bare dated string.  The two OTHER places that record this database --
# marker_manifest.tsv, and the Tier-2 caches' own amrfinder_database_version -- keep the
# plain dated string on purpose: they record what a tool printed, and asking them to
# carry our digest would make point 1 and point 2 fail instead of tightening them.  A
# row with no database_digest (every bundled database) keeps the bare version, because
# the lockfile already pins its bytes and point 1 checks that.
# The honest limit of the whole freeze: a digest proves SAMENESS, not availability.  It
# cannot make NCBI serve 2026-05-15.1 again.  If the archived copy of the dated
# directory is lost after NCBI has moved on, the pinned database is unrecoverable, and
# the manifest can then only prove that whatever is on disk is not it.
# HOW TO ADD A ROW
#   1. before the change:  update_gate.py --panel --out before.tsv
#   2. after the change:   update_gate.py --panel --out after.tsv
#   3.                     update_gate.py --compare before.tsv after.tsv
#      That prints the class of every moved call and refuses any it cannot attribute.
#   4. Add one row per moved component with the totals and digest it reports, then
#      re-run update_gate.py --check.
# A `panel` row is the one class that records no tool difference.  It records a change
# to WHICH evidence the gate replays, and its from/to are panel scope identities rather
# than tool identities.  It exists because the panel's scope has to be able to move
# legally: curation that shrinks or grows it must have a row to add, or the gate is a
# dead end that only hand-editing history can clear.
# THE ROWS BELOW ARE THE FIRST RECORDING of all 38 components, all dated 2026-08-04:
# every one starts from `-` and moved no calls.  Their reviewer is `initial-pin`
# because no human decision sits behind a first recording; every LATER row must name
# the person who reviewed the change.  One extra row belongs to that same first
# recording and so carries the same reviewer: db:amrfinderplus is written twice on the
# same date, once as the bare dated label and once with the roll-up digest of its 162
# files folded in.  Three rows carry a finding rather than a plain first pin --
# tool:sistr (an environment that had drifted from its own lockfile and was put back),
# db:amrfinderplus (a dated database that no lockfile can capture) and panel:scope (a
# scope that must be frozen, because reading it from the ledger lets ordinary curation
# move it) -- and their notes say so.
date

The one dated, post-install database in the tree: it lives outside the conda package, so no lockfile can capture it. FROZEN on 2026-08-04, because `amrfinder -u` only ever fetches the LATEST database and nothing can ask NCBI for a dated one -- all 162 files (239.4 MB) are digested in src/curation-triage/amrfinderplus_db_manifest.tsv, roll-up sha256 2fb16b7f3c57..., recorded as database_digest in tool_pins.tsv. setup_envs.sh provisions it into the pinned prefix and checks BOTH `amrfinder --database_version` against this value and every file against that manifest, naming any that differ. The identity below folds the roll-up digest into the dated string, so the gate fails on a database swapped under an unchanged version. Sameness is all a digest can prove: if the local archive is lost, this version cannot be downloaded again.
A PubMLST copy frozen inside the package on 2023-07-07; it cannot be refreshed without changing the build.

The O/H allele set and the pathotype table are bundled, but the MASH species sketch is a run-time Zenodo download that nothing pins. That is why the kind is runtime-download and why ECTyper stays context-only.
Bundled with the package; the date is what the shipped database calls itself.

The 144 PubMLST schemes bundled in the 2.23.0 build, including listeria_2 and ypseudotuberculosis_achtman_3. 144 is what `mlst --list` reports; db/pubmlst holds 145 entries, but one of them (dbases.sh) is a helper script, not a scheme.
Bundled with the package, so the lockfile pins the data as well as the code.
Bundled with the package. The installed dist-info disagrees with the conda build about the version, so the build string is the identity that can be trusted.
The bundled sistr.msh; no flag reports its version, so it is read from the package's own dbstatus.txt.

Which units the validation panel replays: the 21 confounded units plus the 20 Tier-1 leads standing at frozen in PANEL_SCOPE in bin/curation-triage/update_gate.py. It is pinned rather than read from ledger.ndjson because a scope taken from curation data moves underneath the gate: an SME resolving a lead shrinks the panel, moves its digest and fails the gate with no row anyone could legally add, since no pin moved and a row may not record from == to. Adding or removing a unit is a reviewed decision recorded here as a `panel` row.
How markers.py reads BTyper3's genomospecies and marker profile into a verdict about the B. cereus group.
How markers.py reads AMRFinderPlus's bont hits into a botulinum group and toxin type.
How markers.py reads ECTyper's serotype and pathotype. Context only today: it decides no verdict, so no panel call depends on it yet.
The screen applied to a unit whose taxon has no dedicated task. Never auto-triggered, so it decides no panel call today.
How markers.py combines LisSero's serogroup with the classical MLST ST/CC, keeping them as separate un-merged fields.
How markers.py reconciles SISTR's cgMLST subspecies with SeqSero2's antigenic serovar.
How markers.py reads ShigEiFinder's cluster call into a Shigella / EIEC / E. coli verdict.
How markers.py reads the plasmid pre-screen and the classical MLST context. The cgMLST classifier this task really needs is a recorded gap, so the rule can only return indeterminate.
Identity and coverage floors the BTyper3 reading applies, as declared in marker_manifest.tsv.
Identity and coverage floors for the bont hits.
Identity and coverage floors for the ECTyper reading.
Identity and coverage floors for the two generic screens.
Floors for the serogroup, the classical MLST (exact match) and the cgMLST/LIN component that is still a gap.
Identity and coverage floors for the SISTR and SeqSero2 readings.
Identity and coverage floors for the ShigEiFinder reading.

The species boundary, the aligned-fraction gate, the dereplication line, the borderline band and skani's own screen floors. These live in code (tier2.py, skani_runner.py), so without this row a moved boundary would be an unattributable difference.
Floors for the plasmid pre-screen, the exact-match classical MLST and the cgMLST component that is still a gap.
A Perl script: the prefix bin has to be first on PATH or it dies on a missing Path::Tiny, which reads like a broken install and is not one.
Software only. Its dated database moves independently and is pinned separately as db:amrfinderplus.
The seq_*_db resources and the PubMLST copy travel inside the package, so this build pins that data as well as the code.
From conda-forge, not bioconda, unlike every other pin. Used only to build the Tier-1 datasets cache; an offline replay never runs it.
Context-only: no decisive task routes it, which is why its 943 MiB Zenodo sketch is deliberately not provisioned. A panel call that depended on it would fail point 1.
Shells out to makeblastdb from the same prefix, so the pin covers the BLAST+ build too.
One prefix serves both typers.py tool keys, mlst_listeria and mlst_yersinia; they differ only by --scheme, so there is one artifact and one pin.
The executable keeps its .py suffix (SeqSero2_package.py), so the binary name is not the tool name.
`shigeifinder --version` exits 2 and prints usage, so the conda build is the only checkable identity and every call records shigeifinder@unknown.

Recorded as unchanged after a real investigation: the installed prefix carried an unowned setuptools-83.0.0 egg-info while conda-meta and the lockfile both said 80.10.2. The environment was made to match its lockfile, sistr's calls were re-run before and after and came out byte-identical, and the regenerated lockfile is identical to this one. So no pin moved and this is a baseline row, not a change row.
Supplies the ANI and aligned fraction behind every Tier-2 comparison. marker_manifest.tsv does not list it because it answers no marker question, but its version moves calls.

The database identity became more precise: the dated label gained the roll-up sha256 of its 162 files, so a database swapped under an unchanged version string is now a gate failure and not only a setup_envs.sh failure. No call moved -- `--compare` reports 1 pinned component moved, 75 calls before, 75 after, 0 changed -- because the bytes are the same database; only what we record about it changed. Restoring it needs the archived tarball; NCBI serves only the latest.
